title: Structured streaming glitch: customer handbook & quickchecks
content:
Purpose
This handbook-style update is intended for tenants and technical contacts who saw degraded structured streaming responses between 2026-11-04 02:14 UTC and 2026-11-04 03:40 UTC. It combines a short status page style update, a compact timeline, a technical summary suitable for engineers, and step-by-step quickchecks customers can run to validate recovery for their integrations.

Short status (one-line)
We observed partial degradation of structured streaming responses in a subset of EU-hosted inference clusters; services were restored to normal by 2026-11-04 03:40 UTC.

Impact summary
- Scope: ~0.7% of active tenant streaming sessions routed to EU region during the window experienced truncated or delayed structured output tokens (JSON/DELIMITED formats).
- Symptoms observed by customers: truncated structured outputs, missing trailing fields in streamed JSON, occasionally duplicate EOS tokens mid-stream.
- Severity: customer-facing but limited (most non-streaming calls and other regions unaffected).

Compact timeline (UTC)
- 2026-11-04 02:14 — First alerts: elevated error-rate for structured streaming encoding observed by internal monitors (trace id sampling).
- 2026-11-04 02:18 — On-call SRE escalated; routing isolation activated for suspect node pools.
- 2026-11-04 02:25 — Initial mitigation: automatic rollbacks of a runtime kernel selector patch begun in affected AZ.
- 2026-11-04 02:47 — Partial recovery observed; error-rate trending down but intermittent truncation continued.
- 2026-11-04 03:05 — Engineers deployed targeted hotfix that corrected a KV-cache boundary check causing early token flushes.
- 2026-11-04 03:40 — Metrics normalized to baseline; SLOs validated.

High-level root cause (engineer-friendly)
- Summary: A kernel-selection optimization (landed 2026-11-03) interacted with structured-streaming flush semantics when the downstream client asked for delimited JSON tokens that crossed an internal KV-cache boundary. The combination caused the runtime to emit an EOS/flush marker prematurely for some sequences, resulting in truncated streamed payloads or duplicate terminators. The bug was deterministic for specific sequence-length/quantization combos.

What we did (actions taken)
- Immediate: Isolated the affected node pool and routed new requests to compatible pools to avoid further customer exposure.
- Rollback: Reverted the kernel selector change in EU node pool instances where degradation was manifest.
- Hotfix: Applied a guard in the streaming flush path to respect delimited-token boundaries across KV-cache buckets and added unit + integration tests.
- Validation: Ran canonical prompt sets and customer-submitted failing snippets through the patched runtime; validated token-level parity with expected structured outputs.

Current status (as of last_modified)
- Service: Normal in all regions. No ongoing truncation incidents reported after 03:40 UTC.
- Monitoring: Additional synthetic streaming checks deployed to EU and global canaries.
- Ticketing: Root cause ticketed and being expanded into a postmortem with remediation tasks.

Customer quickchecks (how to verify from your side)
Run the following steps to confirm your tenant did not retain truncated outputs and that integrations are healthy:
1) Replay a small sample of streaming prompts (the same prompt shape that you observed issues with). Compare streamed tokens to a non-streaming (batch) run — final JSON payloads should match token-by-token after assembly.
2) If you use structured-delimited mode, validate: a) no premature EOS token in middle of expected JSON; b) closing delimiter (e.g., '}}' or ']\")' or supplied terminator) appears in the final token batch.
3) For SDK users: upgrade to SDK >= 3.2.7 (hotfix-compatible client) and retry streaming to ensure client-side assembly is tolerant of now-fixed flush semantics.
4) If you still observe anomalies, capture a trace_id from the response headers (x-rw-trace-id) and submit it to support with a short description and timestamp.

Evidence bundle we can provide on request
- Per-tenant trace logs (sampled traces for sessions in window) — JIRA-INC-2026-3145 attachment list.
- Before/after token diffs for canonical failing prompts (engineer-run artifacts).
- Patch diff and unit/integration test outputs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/452).

Recommended immediate customer actions
- If you operate long-lived streaming sessions with structured delimiters: restart active streams opened before 03:40 UTC on 2026-11-04 (this guarantees any affected in-flight sessions are fully re-established under the patched runtime).
- If you require evidence for compliance: request a tenant-specific evidence package (we will include traces and signed verification).
- For mission-critical integrations: consider enabling multi-region routing (failover) or dedicated pools for peak windows until the postmortem completes. Our SREs can assist in setup.

Notes on credits/compensation
- We are evaluating tenant impact and will follow existing SLA/credits policies where appropriate. Customer Success will reach out to impacted accounts with estimated credit calculations based on affected request counts.

FAQ (short)
Q: Will my stored data have been modified?
A: No. This incident affected streaming output emission; it did not mutate stored tenant data or cached artifacts.

Q: Could this happen again?
A: The immediate fix and unit/integration tests reduce regression risk. Postmortem will include additional guardrails (including canary limits for kernel selector changes and forced synthetic coverage for structured streaming).

Planned follow-up
- 2026-11-06: Full internal postmortem published to Confluence (link will be shared).
- 2026-11-09: Customer-facing postmortem summary and remediation timeline delivered to impacted tenants.

Contact and escalation
- Primary CS contact: Asha Patel (asha@redwood.ai) — customer success lead for impacted accounts.
- SRE lead: Marcus Liu (marcus@redwood.ai) — technical escalations and evidence coordination.
- For urgent operational needs: open a high-priority support ticket referencing JIRA-INC-2026-3145 and include x-rw-trace-id when possible.

Internal notes / loose ends (for CS/SRE collaboration)
- Verify SDK bundles are updated in CDN within 24h of hotfix publication.
- Add targeted synthetic prompts to the global canary suite that exercise KV-cache boundary tokenization.
- Schedule optional office hours with impacted enterprise tenants to walk the evidence bundle (invite list in Confluence).

Prepared by: Asha Patel (customer-success)
Reviewed: Marcus Liu, Sofia Hernandez, Ben Carter

Document status: in_review — intended to be used as a customer-facing statuspage + an engineer-friendly evidence handbook for immediate tenant verification and support triage.
